name: U.S. Federation of Worker Cooperatives
description: The national membership organization for worker cooperatives in the US, advancing worker-owned and worker-governed workplaces through education, technical assistance, and advocacy. Founded in 2004 out of a national gathering of regional worker-co-op practitioners. Represents nearly 450 business and organizational members, standing in for an estimated 1,300 US worker co-ops and roughly 15,000 workers. Governed by a 100% member-elected board; offices in Oakland, CA and Philadelphia, PA. Co-hosts the annual Worker Co-op Conference with the Democracy at Work Institute.

research.notes: Re-checked 2026-10-21 for the recurrence backfill, opening each council and peer-network event page rather than relying on the September pass — which had called them all member-oriented, and was wrong for most of them. Added as recurring events: the Worker Cooperative Startup Webinar (first Wednesdays; converted from a single 2026-10-07 record), the Union Co-ops Council's public call, and the Media Co-ops, Black Cooperator, and Cannabis Co-ops peer networks — Media and Black Cooperator say outright that non-members are welcome. Left out: the Policy & Advocacy Council (its calls are "for all members", and registering adds you to a member listserv), the Immigrant Movement in Co-ops council (a Spanish-language meeting of representatives of immigrant-led co-ops, with no cadence published), and the Annual Member Meeting and Worker Benefits webinar, which are for members. The Racial & Economic Justice council has no meeting on the current calendar. Forums: the Worker Co-op Slack and the Spanish-language WhatsApp group are both still listed on the Connect page.
